title: Book One · Chapter 125: Two Sides of a Street
story:
Mei puts her drawing on the classroom floor. It is too wide for her desk. There are shops on both sides of a road. Little people stand at the doors.

Ronan sits down beside it.

“Our gate is wrong.”

“That is not your gate.”

“It is green.”

“Other people have green gates.”

Leo comes over and looks from the other side.

“The river is missing.”

“The river is behind you,” Mei says. “You are sitting on it.”

Leo moves at once. Then he sees there is no river on the floor. Mei laughs and puts her pencil down. She cannot draw while she is laughing.

Miss Wu asks them to put the drawing on two desks. She wants to see the whole drawing. The children move out of her way.

“This is the street by my aunt's home,” Mei explains. “I know these places. I am drawing them.”

Ronan takes his new drawing from his bag. It shows Mr Qiu's old stall and the crates. He has changed the words. The story about money is gone.

Miss Wu reads the short line.

“May we put this beside Mei's picture?”

“I have to ask Mr Qiu again.”

She gives it back to him. “Then leave a space for it.”

Ronan looks at the empty part of the wall. It is not a very large space. His drawing would fit easily. He wants to put his picture there now. But Mr Qiu has not agreed to that yet.

At home he shows Mr Qiu the paper. Mr Qiu reads it at his table. Then a customer comes to buy a rubber. Ronan waits for Mr Qiu to give her change.

“My pencils are in a dry place,” Mr Qiu reads. “Yes.”

“Can it go on our classroom wall?”

“For how long?”

“I don't know.”

“Who can see it?”

“Our class. Miss Wu. Perhaps other teachers.”

Mr Qiu taps the part with the crates.

“Ask those things first.”

The next morning Ronan asks. “The pictures can stay for two weeks,” Miss Wu says. They will be inside the classroom. She will ask the children before another class visits.

Ronan writes this on the back of his sheet. He takes it to Mr Qiu after school.

“Two weeks,” the old man says. “That is all right.”

“And your name?”

“Still mine. You may use it.”

Ronan checks the words once more at breakfast. Dad reaches for the paper, then waits until Ronan gives it to him. He reads it and points to a little dark mark near the crates.

“What is that?”

“His cup.”

“I thought it was another child.”

Ronan puts a handle on the cup. Dad can see it now. Dad adds no words of his own. He gives the paper back. Ronan rolls the paper with the picture inside. Now he can carry it safely to school.

When the drawing goes up, Mei moves her own picture a little to make room. Ronan holds one corner for her.

“Your street has more people,” he says.

“I know more people there.”

“Will you draw River Street?”

“Perhaps. I want to show people at work and play. Not just standing in doors.”

Ronan looks at Mr Qiu in his picture. The old man is standing beside a crate, doing nothing. He takes out a pencil.

“I can give him his sign.”

Mei brings her chair nearer. She points to the hand in his drawing. He draws the sign just below it. Mr Qiu looks busier already. Ronan likes that. Mr Qiu can sell his pencils now. Ronan wants to show that in his picture. His picture does not need the private story too.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：make room＝腾出位置；for how long＝持续多久；beside＝在旁边。

情节提示：aunt＝姑、姨等女性长辈；rubber＝橡皮；customer＝顾客。

理解：1. Ronan 为什么两次去问 Mr Qiu？2. Mei 想怎样画街上的人？
